Linear combination of vectors, linearly dependent and independent vectors

card.title: Dot, cross and triple products — algebra with direction

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Vectors add tip-to-tail; their products split three ways: dot product (scalar — projection, work, angle finder), cross product (vector — area, normal direction), scalar triple product (scalar — volume, coplanarity test). Linear dependence asks whether one vector hides inside the span of others; independent sets build bases. Collinear/coplanar describe living on shared lines/planes.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: a·b = |a||b|cosθ = a₁b₁+a₂b₂+a₃b₃  ·  |a×b| = |a||b|sinθ (area of parallelogram)  ·  [abc] = a·(b×c) = determinant (volume; = 0 ⟺ coplanar)  ·  projection of a on b: (a·b)/|b|  ·  a=(2,−1,4), b=(1,2,−2): a·b = 2−2−8 = −8, |b| = 3 → projection −8/3

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Dot/cross need the ANGLE between vectors tail-to-tail. Triple product needs exactly three 3D vectors; cyclic order preserves sign, swaps flip it. Dependence tests solve c₁v₁ + c₂v₂ + … = 0 — only the trivial solution means independence. Projection divides by |b| (non-zero b).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: a = 2i+3j−k, b = i−j+2k: a·b = 2−3−2 = −3; a×b = determinant → (5, −5, −5), magnitude 5√3 (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Scalar projection of (2,−1,4) on (1,2,−2): −8/3 — negative means against b's direction (NEB 2023 MCQ). Three vectors coplanar ⟺ triple product zero.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: a·b for a = 2i+3j−k, b = i−j+2k: multiply components and add → 2(1) + 3(−1) + (−1)(2) = −3. Cross: |i j k; 2 3 −1; 1 −1 2| = i(6−1) − j(4+1) + k(−2−3) = 5i − 5j − 5k, |a×b| = √(25+25+25) = 5√3 (NEB 2023, 3 marks). Sign-check: obtuse angle (negative dot) matches.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Dot product loses direction (many vectors share one projection). Cross product exists only in 3D (and 7D exotically). Triple-product zero proves coplanarity, not which vector depends on which. Component formulas assume orthonormal î, ĵ, k̂.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Dot from the cosine rule: |a−b|² = |a|²+|b|²−2|a||b|cosθ expands component-wise to leave a·b = Σaᵢbᵢ — algebra meets geometry. Cross magnitude as parallelogram area: base|height| = |a||b|sinθ. Triple product as determinant: expanding along rows gives the signed volume; zero volume flattens to a plane (coplanar test proved).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Angle questions → dot product first. Area/normal questions → cross. 'Coplanar?' → triple-product determinant = 0. Projection sign tells direction sense (negative = against). Position-vector problems: AB = b − a (tip minus tail), then compute.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (3): a·b and |a×b| for (2,3,−1), (1,−1,2). NEB 2023 (1): scalar projection −8/3 (MCQ). NEB 2022 (2): scalar triple product + geometric meaning. NEB 2022 (3): position vector from A and B.
